biography.plain_text: Carlo Traglio is an Italian jeweller and art collector who developed Vhernier after his family acquired the company in 2001. From a family of Coca-Cola bottlers, he trained in goldsmithing and studied law before joining the family business. At Vhernier, he combined contemporary design with the traditions of Italian jewellery craftsmanship.

confidence.reason: Trade-association and museum biographies establish training and career; company acquisition history is independently confirmed.

biography.html: Carlo Traglio is an Italian jeweller and art collector who developed Vhernier after his family acquired the company in 2001. From a family of Coca-Cola bottlers, he trained in goldsmithing and studied law before joining the family business. At Vhernier, he combined contemporary design with the traditions of Italian jewellery craftsmanship.

long_biography.plain_text:
A drawing by David Hockney tested Carlo Traglio's determination as a young collector. His father refused to pay for it, but he bought it anyway. The Italian jeweller had begun collecting at about sixteen, saving money, borrowing and paying for works in instalments. Museum visits helped him discover artists whose work he later sought out.

His interest extended beyond acquiring paintings. At Loft Vhernier in Milan, he displayed works suitable for a public space and hosted exhibitions, a photography auction and installations made for the venue. His jewellery business also produced a medal designed by Cy Twombly for the American Academy, adapting the artist's design to the practical demands of goldsmithing.

confidence.reason: Full direct collecting interview supports the personal episode, acquisition practices, venue activities and specific medal collaboration.
